tier_reason: C stands: third-party shootout, not like for like; enricher corrects two caveats.

corrections.caveats: Enricher corrections: on caveat 4, UTF-8 validation outside the Rust timer is not an asymmetry against default RapidJSON, whose default kParseNoFlags leaves kParseValidateEncodingFlag off; it is an asymmetry only against parsers that validate inside the timer. On caveat 2, RapidJSON built without SSE is not an advantage taken by serde_json, whose parse_whitespace is also byte by byte with no SIMD (issue #120 open since 2016); it only means RapidJSON is not at its best configuration. Gotchas: 128-level nesting limit (#1327); from_reader is slow without a BufReader (#160: 23 MiB file, 4710 ms unbuffered vs 55 ms from_str); from_slice vs from_str on twitter.json struct decode 2.290 vs 1.384 ms (sonic-rs README); serde_json::Value maps are BTreeMaps with heavy memory use (#635); 1.0.147 replaced Ryu with Zmij for float output, changing printed floats (#1309, #1340 open); untagged and flatten buffer through Content (#2101: 484 vs 181 us) and break arbitrary_precision (#721, #1108).

corrections.caveats: Enricher: the evidence is the same kostya Json rows as the serde_json entry, so it measures serde's derive pattern through serde_json only; no comparison against cereal or Boost.Serialization (the category's C++ baselines) was found. Untagged enums and flatten buffer through an intermediate Content value (#2101: 484 vs 181 us) and break serde_json's arbitrary_precision (#721, #1108).
